title.narrative: EA 15/2011 - South Sudan: Access to Basic services for Returnees, IDPs and other vulnerable populat

description.narrative:
The aim of the project will be twofold: responding to the needs of the vulnerable population in the 7 diocese within South Sudan and capacity building of the local and national partners (the diocesan development offices & Sudan aid respectively). The activities will deal with the emergency needs and improving access to basic services targeting vulnerable communities and households in all areas of operations; The activities to implemented are; • Emergency preparedness and response • Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Promotion • Shelter and Non-Food Items • Food Security • Health • Capacity building • Education • Peace building The project will also provide tailor-made trainings to National and Diocesan Sudan Aid Offices that will improve their organizational and program delivery capacities (i.e. community based disaster risk reduction, MQ trainings). In addition, Sudan Aid Offices will be actively involved in the program delivery alongside CARITAS member organizations, which will enable the Sudan Aid office to putt newly acquired skills into practice. The project will put emphasis on local ownership and responsibility for the program design and delivery with local diocesan partners. From the previous appeal EA12/2010; it was noted that the scope of assistance has to be wider than just emergency response; the focus needs to be on implementing activities that will create a positive and lasting change in the lives of beneficiaries.
The direct beneficiaries of the project will be the staff working in the 7 Dioceses in South Sudan, National Sudan aid staff based in South Sudan and Caritas coordination unit managing the appeal .Potentially up to 100,000 direct beneficiaries will be targeted in the 7 diocese beside in direct beneficiaries within the Communities in the targeted dioceses that will also benefit through participation in emergency preparedness, response, recovery & rehabilitation activities. The project will be managed by a Caritas Coordination Unit, and will involve staff from Sudan aid, the Dioceses, and participating CI agencies. CAFOD will participate in the programme steering committee alongside CRS and the national Sudanaid, and will “twin” with 2 dioceses to facilitate appeal activities at diocesan and community level: Yei and Tombura-Yambio.
This contribution to the overall project will target the salaries for staff implementing activities in Yei and Juba diocese activities included are WASH, NFIs and food distribution and emergency preparedness and response training with emphasis in CMDRR.
